newsitem.title: NORWAY: POLL-Norway premier favoured to win election.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Norway premier favoured to win election.

text.p: Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland, who heads Norway's Labour minority government, is the most popular politician ahead of the country's elections in September, according to an opinion poll released on Tuesday.
The survey, commissioned by the daily Arbeiderbladet, said 41 percent of the voters preferred Jagland as prime minister to his two official challengers Kjell Magne Bondevik and Johan J. Jakobsen.

It said Bondevik, who is prime minister candidate for the Christian People's Party, received support from 22 percent of the respondents while only nine percent favoured Jakobsen, the Centre Party's candidate for the job. The remaining 28 percent were undecided.
The survey was carried out in June by ACNielsen, one of the country's six major pollsters.
"Thorbjoern Jagland has got solid backing as the most popular candidate for the position of prime minister ahead of the elections this autumn," Arbeiderbladet said in a comment.
The Labour Party is by far the biggest among the eight parties represented in the 165-seat Storting, or parliament.

The main threat to Jagland's government in the September 15 vote comes from the three centrist parties -- the Christian People's Party, the Centre Party and liberal Venstre -- who want to form a minority coalition government.

The Labour Party, which has been in power since 1990, won 36.9 percent of the votes in the 1993 election. But it received only 30.6 percent of voter support in the latest monthly opinion poll published by daily Aftenposten last month.
It put the total for the three centrist parties at 28.8 percent.

The centrists want to invest more of Norway's oil wealth in schools and public transportation while the Labour government is setting aside the entire budget surplus -- projected at 57.3 billion crowns this year -- in the State Petroleum Fund for investment in overseas securities.
